_meta.indication: Ultrasound contrast agent indicated for use in patients with suboptimal echocardiograms to opacify the left ventricular chamber and to improve the delineation of the left ventricular endocardial border.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Three multi-center controlled clinical trials (Study A, Study B, Study C)
pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center controlled trials in which each patient received randomized-order intravenous bolus injections of Lumason; contrast echocardiography compared to non-contrast (baseline) echocardiography in the same patient, with images evaluated by two independent blinded reviewers.
pivotal_trials.population: 191 patients with suspected cardiac disease and suboptimal non-contrast echocardiography (127 men, 64 women; mean age 59 years).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Improvement in left ventricular endocardial border delineation (and left ventricular opacification) with contrast versus baseline non-contrast echocardiography.
pivotal_trials.n: N=191 (Study A 76, Study B 62, Study C 53)
pivotal_trials.result: In all three studies Lumason improved left ventricular endocardial border delineation; the percentage of patients with inadequate border delineation (Reader A) fell from 79% to 33% in Study A, 50% to 19% in Study B, and 23% to 19% in Study C. Complete left ventricular opacification was observed in 52% to 80% of patients after a 2.0-mL dose.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥0.5%) are headache (0.9%) and nausea (0.6%); overall adverse reactions occurred in 302 (4.9%) of 6179 patients. Serious cardiopulmonary reactions, including fatalities, have occurred uncommonly within 30 minutes of administration (boxed warning). Anaphylactoid reactions have uncommonly been observed.
target_moa: Within the blood, the acoustic impedance of Lumason microspheres is lower than that of surrounding tissue, so an ultrasound beam is reflected from the microsphere/tissue interface; the reflected signal provides a visual image contrasting the blood from surrounding tissues. The microspheres are an SF6 gas core surrounded by a phospholipid monolayer shell.
modality: Other (ultrasound contrast agent: gas-filled lipid microspheres)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SERIOUS CARDIOPULMONARY REACTIONS — Serious cardiopulmonary reactions, including fatalities, have occurred uncommonly during or following injection of ultrasound contrast agents, including sulfur hexafluoride lipid microspheres; most serious reactions occur within 30 minutes of administration.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was needed for this resubmission; the application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant public health questions.

description.text: Added indication for use in echocardiography to opacify the left ventricular chamber and improve left ventricular endocardial border delineation in adult and pediatric patients with suboptimal echocardiograms

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for an additional indication for Lumason, specifically indicated for use in echocardiography to opacify the left ventricular chamber and to improve the delineation of the left ventricular endocardial border in adult and pediatric patients with suboptimal echocardiograms.

summary.text: Lumason was approved as a new molecular entity ultrasound contrast agent via a 505(b)(1) NDA originally submitted December 21, 2011. It received two Complete Response Letters for manufacturing facility deficiencies before the April 11, 2014 resubmission led to approval; no advisory committee meeting was needed and a deferred pediatric study was required under PREA.

citations.quote: Lumason is a new molecular entity classified as an ultrasound contrast agent.

On April 11, 2014 Bracco Diagnostics resubmitted a 505(b)(1) New Drug Application (NDA) for Lumason (sulfur hexafluoride lipid-Type A microsphere) in response to a November 30, 2013 complete response action taken because of manufacturing deficiencies identified by the agency during the inspection of the Bracco manufacturing facility. Evaluate the efficacy of Lumason contrasted echocardiography vs. non-contrast echocardiography for left ventricular border delineation in 92 patients (males and females) 9-17 years old. During the clinical evaluation, pharmacokinetic assessments will be performed on 6 patients, 9-12 years old (3 males and 3 females) and 6 patients 12-17 years old (3 males and 3 females).
